fields.description:
# S8 — Cut the production review bot over to Bedrock Claude (dogfood, no cross-provider fallback)

## Context / Problem

The `LLM-Review` vote gates every landing on `main`, and today it runs against the direct Anthropic
API. The epic's premise is that our clients will predominantly reach Claude through Bedrock, so the
path rebar develops against is not the path rebar's users run; dogfooding closes that gap. State the
premise honestly: it is an asserted product judgement, not a measured one — no survey or citation
backs it anywhere in the epic. What IS measurable is the consequence: if Bedrock throttles,
mis-caches, or returns differently shaped structured output, we find out on our own repo before a
client does.

This ticket was written early in epic 061c and its original Scope and Approach have been overtaken by
the epic's own deliverables. The rewrite below replaces them. What changed:

* the per-pass model split it worried about **now exists in code**, so the cutover is a configuration
  act rather than a design problem;
* the single `REBAR_LLM_MODEL` knob it named is **deprecated** [rebar:eb58-e71d-ec90-4b00] and cannot
  express a per-class mapping, so it is no longer the instrument;
* the `observability.sh` alarm it listed as a deliverable **already shipped** under S4b;
* the Anthropic-key retirement it promised is **not expressible** against the current `.env` layout
  and would break the kill switch it also promises.

## What is already established — do NOT re-measure or re-build

* **The per-pass class split has LANDED.** `src/rebar/llm/workflow/gates/code-review.yaml` now
  declares `base: model: frontier` (:74), `round_a`/`round_b`: `model_ladder: [frontier]` (:92, :130),
  `verify: model: standard` (:174) and `coach: model: standard` (:209); `plan-review.yaml` Pass-1 is
  `model_ladder: [frontier]` (:70-71) and the verifier paths resolve `standard`
  [rebar:172e-b207-4c18-4243, rebar:77ed-dea1-4997-4f74, rebar:7761-4b1a-e8c3-45a0,
  rebar:3768-789c-11ed-48be, rebar:cc33-13db-de48-4468]. The gate no longer reads a single
  `cfg.model` for all four passes. **The obsolete-plan hazard is therefore inverted from what this
  ticket used to say: the risk is no longer "one knob for four passes", it is choosing an instrument
  that COLLAPSES the split that now exists.**
* **No bare `claude-*` id survives on either gate's executed path.** The only remaining bare ids under
  `src/rebar/llm/workflow/` are `examples/review_skeleton.yaml:44` (an example, never executed by the
  bot) and JSX placeholders in `editor_assets/`. The split-brain this ticket previously warned about
  is closed.
* **Escalation no longer crosses providers.** `plan_review/sizing.py:400` `models_at_or_above` maps
  every at-or-above rung through its model class via `_rung_target`, which drops a rung it cannot name
  in the run's provider [rebar:7761-4b1a-e8c3-45a0]. A Bedrock-configured run escalates to Bedrock.
* **`pydantic_ai.exceptions.UserError` is now caught** (`src/rebar/llm/failure.py:250,271`), so a
  Bedrock client-construction failure reaches rebar's typed failure path instead of escaping every
  `except LLMError` handler [rebar:a574-7193-6a5b-48e9].
* **Both region variables are ALREADY SET in the review-bot service.**
  `infra/compose/docker-compose.yml:151` `REBAR_LLM_BEDROCK_REGION: "us-east-1"` and `:157`
  `AWS_DEFAULT_REGION: "us-east-1"`. They are NOT interchangeable and both are required: rebar's own
  knob threads into `BedrockProvider` while botocore reads only `AWS_DEFAULT_REGION`
  (`AWS_REGION` alone does not work on boto3/botocore 1.43.58), and IMDS supplies credentials but never
  a region [rebar:a574-7193-6a5b-48e9]. Verify, do not re-derive.
* **IAM is granted and exercised.** `infra/terraform/iam_s7.tf` grants `bedrock:InvokeModel` +
  `InvokeModelWithResponseStream` on `*.anthropic.claude-*` inference profiles, scoped to the instance
  role, verified by a real call rather than the policy simulator
  [rebar:9249-1569-7be9-4f67].
* **The VOTER_ERROR alarm chain already exists and is live.** `review_bot/voter.py` `_voter_error()`
  writes a greppable line to journald; `infra/scripts/observability.sh` §4 (:113, :135) publishes
  `rebar/host:voter_errors`; `infra/terraform/monitoring_s4b.tf` declares
  `aws_cloudwatch_metric_alarm.voter_errors` = `rebar-gerrit-voter-errors` (`period = 300`,
  `evaluation_periods = 1`, `threshold = 0`, :48-54); `infra/runbooks/review-bot-ops.md:110` documents
  reading it. `describe-alarms` returns `StateValue: OK` with a fresh datapoint. **Nothing in
  `observability.sh` is a deliverable of this story** — an implementer who takes the old Scope at face
  value will rebuild it and may double-publish the metric.
* **Only INFERENCE PROFILES are invokable**, and caching works on them. Plain on-demand
  `anthropic.claude-*` ids return `ValidationException: … on-demand throughput isn't supported`;
  `us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6` measured `cache_write=4017` then read on the next attempt
  [rebar:2932-8a98-6d70-4550]. The verified id triple is checked in at
  `.github/llm-providers/bedrock.toml`.
* **All three local gates already run clean on Bedrock** — `review-plan` (27/27 Bedrock calls,
  `cache_read` 226,668), `review-code` (5/5 Bedrock, `cache_read` 18,292), `verify-completion`
  (1/1 Bedrock, `cache_read` 45,122), all with structured output validating and zero direct-Anthropic
  calls [rebar:1aa2-37cf-5cdf-48b7]. This cutover is a confirmation, not a first contact.
* **The parity bar is cleared as the epic defines it** [rebar:0d76-ebbf-ee3a-48ac]: same payloads,
  same tools, provider-clean routing, both inference profiles invoke. The operator hold recorded on
  this ticket ("DO NOT claim until 0d76 records a cleared bar") is therefore RELEASED. Carry the
  nuance: the residual `gating_failures` are informational cross-model verdict comparisons, so the
  slots read `passed=False` while no acceptance criterion is unmet.

## Approach

Fill the review-bot's **model-class slots** with Bedrock inference-profile ids, in the service's own
`environment:` block in `infra/compose/docker-compose.yml`:

```yaml
      REBAR_LLM_FRONTIER_MODEL: "bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8"
      REBAR_LLM_STANDARD_MODEL: "bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6"
      REBAR_LLM_TRIVIAL_MODEL:  "bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0"
```

These are the literal names in `src/rebar/llm/model_classes.py:105-115`. Because the gates name
classes rather than model ids, filling the slots re-points Pass-1 onto the Bedrock opus profile and
Pass-2/Pass-4 onto the Bedrock sonnet profile in one act, preserving the split that
[rebar:77ed-dea1-4997-4f74] restored and the standing operator rule behind it (standard is the default
for verification/judging; frontier needs justification). No `src/` change is expected. The ids are
copied from `.github/llm-providers/bedrock.toml` so there is exactly one authoritative triple, and a
test pins the two together so they cannot drift.

**The cutover is purely ADDITIVE and the kill switch is purely SUBTRACTIVE.** `REBAR_LLM_MODEL` appears
nowhere under `infra/` today (verified: `grep -rn REBAR_LLM_MODEL infra/` returns nothing), so the bot
currently runs on the built-in class defaults, which resolve to `anthropic:claude-*`. Deleting the three
lines above and recreating the container therefore restores the Anthropic path with no other edit —
the exact both-directions revert already proven token-free in [rebar:1aa2-37cf-5cdf-48b7] AC7.

**THE IMAGE DOES NOT INSTALL THE BEDROCK PROVIDER PACKAGE — a second, non-config deliverable.**
`infra/compose/Dockerfile.reviewbot:83` is `RUN uv sync --locked --no-dev --extra agents --extra
reviewbot`, and `bedrock` is a **distinct extra** that is not in that list (`pyproject.toml:133-135`,
`bedrock = ["pydantic-ai-slim[bedrock]>=1,<2"]`). `src/rebar/llm/bedrock_model.py:60-66` imports
`pydantic_ai.providers.bedrock` and raises `LLMConfigError` when it is absent, so — with no
cross-provider fallback, deliberately — the class-slot flip ALONE would make the first Bedrock call
fail and the `LLM-Review` gate would stop voting on every landing on `main`. The fix is one flag: add
`--extra bedrock` to that `uv sync`.

*The gap is PARTIALLY masked, which is what defeats the obvious probe.* `pyproject.toml:93` is
`reviewbot = ["fastapi", "uvicorn[standard]", "boto3"]`, so the container ALREADY has boto3, and both
region vars and IMDS credentials are already in place. Any probe of the form "can this container reach
Bedrock with boto3?" — including the boto3 region resolution that the provider builder itself
pre-checks at `bedrock_model.py:76-79` — therefore SUCCEEDS on an image that still lacks the provider
module. The dependency is partially satisfied, so the container reads as healthy right up to the first
gate call. The pre-cutover check must probe the IMPORT, not AWS reachability.

*Why this was invisible:* [rebar:1aa2-37cf-5cdf-48b7] proved all three gates clean on Bedrock (33
calls, zero direct-Anthropic) — but LOCALLY, in a dev env whose `[dev]` extra resolves
`pydantic-ai-slim[anthropic,bedrock,openai,retries]`. A local proof cannot see a container packaging
gap.

*The lockfile does NOT need regenerating — checked, not assumed.* `uv.lock` already carries the bedrock
extra fully resolved: the `nava-rebar` entry has
`bedrock = [{ name = "pydantic-ai-slim", extra = ["bedrock"] }]`, and `pydantic-ai-slim` 1.107.1's own
`bedrock` extra resolves to `boto3==1.43.62`, already locked. `uv lock --check` passes against the
committed lock, and `uv sync --locked --no-dev --extra agents --extra reviewbot --extra bedrock
--dry-run` resolves with no drift complaint — so `--locked` is satisfied by the existing lock and no
`uv lock` regeneration is part of this story. One adjacency worth knowing: `uv.lock`'s `[conflicts]`
declares `bedrock` mutually exclusive with `eval` (and `dev` with `eval`); the image installs neither
`eval` nor `dev`, so adding `--extra bedrock` does not trip it.

**THE ANTHROPIC CREDENTIAL IS RETAINED. This story retires the DEFAULT USE, not the credential.**
`infra/scripts/fetch-secrets.sh` is **out of scope and unchanged**, for two independent reasons:

1. *The kill switch needs it.* A recovery path that flips back to Anthropic without a key is a no-op,
   and it would be discovered at exactly the wrong moment. The credential must outlive the cutover.
2. *It is not per-container in the first place.* `fetch-secrets.sh:81` reads `anthropic-api-key` as a
   REQUIRED param and :116 writes `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=` into ONE shared `.env`, which is `env_file` for
   both `review-bot` (docker-compose.yml:113-114) and `opcert` (:196-197); opcert consumes it for its
   own gate LLM ops (:193). "Retire the key for this container" is not expressible against that layout,
   and deleting the line breaks opcert.

So the post-cutover container still carries `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, deliberately, unused. The old
acceptance criterion asserting the container env contains **no** `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is **withdrawn**:
it contradicted the kill switch, and it was the wrong oracle anyway. The property actually worth
proving is positive and measurable — that no call on the Bedrock path reaches Anthropic — and
`REBAR_USAGE_LOG`'s per-call tally proves it directly, as it did for all three local gates.

**No cross-provider fallback**, unchanged from the original plan and still the right call: a
`FallbackModel` to direct Anthropic would mask exactly the failures this cutover exists to surface, and
a persistently degraded Bedrock could run unnoticed behind it. Note the asymmetry that makes this
coherent rather than dogmatic: the INTRA-provider fallback chain accepted in
[rebar:cc33-13db-de48-4468] (`model_classes.py:388`) stays available; it is only the cross-provider hop
that is refused.

**The transient-fault posture on Bedrock, stated accurately.** The original plan claimed "the existing
tenacity transport retry absorbs transient faults". That is false on this path.
`src/rebar/llm/bedrock_model.py:88` is `return BedrockProvider(region_name=region)` and its docstring
says so explicitly: "No custom client/transport is opened here (unlike the retrying Anthropic path)".
There is no `botocore.config.Config(retries=…)`, no `"adaptive"` mode and no `aws_read_timeout`
anywhere in `src/rebar/llm/` — the tenacity envelope and `RetryConfig` live only in
`anthropic_model.py:114-150`. So:

* Bedrock's transient-fault handling is **botocore's stock client defaults**, which do retry throttling
  and transient 5xx, but are NOT configured by rebar and are NOT driven by `llm_retry_max_attempts` or
  `timeout_s`.
* The epic's "first_class = full fidelity ⇒ equivalent retry and timeout per transport" is an **unmet
  intention, not a landed property**. This story does not claim it and does not fix it: closing it means
  changing the provider builder, which belongs in a `src/` ticket rather than inside a production
  cutover. It is filed as its own defect, linked `discovered_from` this ticket, and the posture is
  written into the runbook so an operator debugging a throttle is not looking for a retry envelope that
  does not exist.
* Related honesty correction: inference profiles are **not** a throttling mitigation, which is how the
  original Approach justified them. Zero throttle events were observed across ~1,400 parity requests,
  the 33 local gate calls, and a 19-call plan-review. The evidenced reason is simpler and stronger —
  on-demand ids are not invokable at all [rebar:2932-8a98-6d70-4550].

**Provenance oracle: `e951` is a hard prerequisite.** [rebar:343b-4fdc-6722-469b] delivered
`provider_provenance` for the plan-review and completion gates only. The code-review gate — the one
that produces the `LLM-Review` vote — still does not stamp it: `code_review/finalize.py:245` sets
`model` and nothing sets `provenance`, while `code_review/sidecar.py:106` reads
`verdict.get("provider_provenance")` and gets `None`. [rebar:e951-7df6-1851-4d5e] fixes exactly this
and is already implemented and pushed as Gerrit change 1307, so depending on it is cheap. The
`provider == "bedrock"` criterion below is gated on e951 landing; the `REBAR_USAGE_LOG` tally is an
independent second observation that does not depend on it, so the cutover is not un-evidenced if e951
slips.

**Alternatives rejected**

* **`REBAR_LLM_MODEL` re-pointed at a Bedrock id** — the original plan's instrument. Rejected on three
  independent grounds: it is deprecated with a migration window [rebar:eb58-e71d-ec90-4b00,
  rebar:d23e-1012-6749-4181], its deprecation shim fans a single value out to ALL THREE classes, which
  collapses the Pass-1/Pass-2 split back into one model, and a scalar cannot express a per-class mapping
  at all. Concretely: sonnet-everywhere silently downgrades the Pass-1 finder; opus-everywhere loses the
  Pass-2 cost downgrade and renders the `temperature: 0` greedy pin at `code-review.yaml:185`
  inoperative, since Bedrock opus accepts only the default temperature. Both single-model outcomes are
  wrong, in opposite directions. A runbook naming it would also rot at v1.0.0.
* **`REBAR_LLM_CONFIG_FILE` pointed at `/app/.github/llm-providers/bedrock.toml`** — genuinely
  attractive: it is the instrument [rebar:1aa2-37cf-5cdf-48b7] proved end-to-end, it is what the CI
  provider matrix uses, and it makes the id triple single-sourced by construction. Rejected for the
  container specifically. The file is present in the image only incidentally —
  `Dockerfile.reviewbot:82` is `COPY . /app` and `.dockerignore` happens not to exclude `.github` — so a
  future context-trimming change would delete it and the pointer would fail at gate time in production,
  after the deploy that caused it. Env class slots also OUTRANK the file pointer in the precedence order
  (CLI > env > `REBAR_LLM_CONFIG_FILE` > discovered file > default), so keeping both layers live invites
  two configurations that silently disagree. The single-sourcing benefit is recovered by the drift test
  instead of by indirection.
* **Per-service Anthropic key retirement via a `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: ""` override in the review-bot
  `environment:` block** — technically expressible (compose `environment:` outranks `env_file`), and it
  would satisfy the old "no Anthropic credential in this container" criterion without touching opcert.
  Rejected because it disables the kill switch for the sake of a criterion we have withdrawn, and buys
  nothing: the credential is unused either way, and "unused" is what the usage-log tally proves.

## Scope

- `infra/compose/docker-compose.yml` — the three class-slot env vars in the `review-bot` service's
  `environment:` block. Region vars are already present and are not re-added.
- `infra/compose/Dockerfile.reviewbot` — add `--extra bedrock` to the `uv sync --locked` line (:83),
  so the image contains `pydantic_ai.providers.bedrock`. No `uv.lock` edit accompanies it (see
  Approach: the lock already resolves that extra and `--locked` is already satisfied).
- `infra/terraform/` — a Bedrock `InvokeModel` client-error alarm built on AWS/Bedrock NATIVE metrics via
  a `metric_query` metric-math expression, NOT a host-published custom metric. MEASURED in this account:
  the `AWS/Bedrock` namespace already publishes `InvocationClientErrors` and `Invocations`, dimensioned by
  `ModelId` (values include `us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6` from this epic's own traffic), so the rate is
  computable as `InvocationClientErrors / Invocations` with no publisher to add. THIS IS WHY
  `observability.sh` STAYS OUT OF SCOPE: the alternative — a `rebar/host` custom metric — would require a
  new publisher there and would re-open a scope claim this plan deliberately makes. It also means the
  DIMENSIONLESS-ON-BOTH-SIDES contract that `monitoring_s4b.tf` and `monitoring_s5.tf` document does not
  apply here: those are host-published custom metrics, whereas a native metric is dimensioned by AWS and
  the alarm must MATCH that dimensioning (`ModelId`) rather than avoid it. State the dimension explicitly
  in the resource so it cannot silently stop matching.
  This is the one signal the existing
  `rebar-gerrit-voter-errors` alarm cannot give: `voter_errors` fires only when the gate fails to vote
  at all, so a partially degraded Bedrock that still produces votes is invisible to it. Thresholds per
  the epic's criterion (client-error rate > 25% of invocations over a 15-minute window, 2 consecutive
  periods), with the alarm ARN and a forced test notification recorded on this ticket — the evidence
  gap the epic's AC has been carrying unresolved.
- `infra/runbooks/` — the kill-switch entry (class slots, not `REBAR_LLM_MODEL`), stating that the
  Anthropic credential is retained by design and why, and recording the actual Bedrock retry/timeout
  posture.
- a test pinning the compose class-slot values to `.github/llm-providers/bedrock.toml`.
- **NOT in scope:** `infra/scripts/fetch-secrets.sh` (see Approach), `infra/scripts/observability.sh`
  (already shipped under S4b), and any `src/rebar/llm/` change — including the botocore retry/timeout
  parity gap, which is filed separately.

## Testing

Live end-to-end, because this is a cutover of a production gate: the oracle is a real vote on a real
change, not a local invocation. The drift test is the only unit-tier item.

- **container packaging, pre-cutover:** rebuild the review-bot image from the amended
  `Dockerfile.reviewbot` and run
  `docker compose exec review-bot python -c "import pydantic_ai.providers.bedrock"`, capturing the exit
  status and output. This runs BEFORE the class slots are set, so a missing provider package surfaces as
  a build-time finding rather than as a gate outage. What is probed is the IMPORT; a boto3/AWS
  reachability probe is not a substitute (see Approach).
- **safety net, pre-cutover:** induce a real `VOTER_ERROR` on the CURRENT Anthropic path and observe
  `rebar-gerrit-voter-errors` transition `OK → ALARM`. Access for this is confirmed (CloudWatch read
  plus SSM to the prod host). Design caveat: per [rebar:c943-1b38-d613-4013] a 409 "change is closed"
  deliberately does NOT emit `VOTER_ERROR`, so a closed change is the wrong way to induce one.
- **happy path:** a test change pushed to `refs/for/main` receives an `LLM-Review` vote; its sidecar
  provenance names `provider == "bedrock"` (requires [rebar:e951-7df6-1851-4d5e]); and independently,
  the run's `REBAR_USAGE_LOG` per-call tally shows every call on a Bedrock inference profile, zero
  direct-Anthropic calls, and the frontier/standard classes resolving to the opus/sonnet profiles
  respectively. Write the usage log to a durable path outside the job workspace — evidence from a live
  gate run has been lost to process death on this host before.
- **failure path, fault injection at the real seam:** temporarily deny the Bedrock IAM statement, push
  a change, and confirm the bot emits `VOTER_ERROR`, casts no false `+1`, and the alarm fires — then
  restore and confirm a clean retry produces a normal vote.
- **recovery:** execute the kill switch once, post-cutover, and confirm a real vote is produced on the
  Anthropic path; then re-apply the cutover.
- **comparison:** the same change reviewed pre- and post-cutover, findings compared.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] ORDERING — THE SAFETY NET IS PROVEN BEFORE THE MODEL FLIP, not alongside it. RATIONALE: this
      cutover removes cross-provider fallback from the gate that reviews EVERY landing on `main`, so if
      Bedrock degrades, landings stop until a human runs the kill switch; a recovery path must be proven
      before it can be needed. Stated accurately against what exists: the `VOTER_ERROR` alarm chain
      ALREADY SHIPPED under S4b and is live, so its half of this criterion is a VERIFICATION task, not a
      build task — do not rebuild `observability.sh` or re-declare the metric. What must land and be
      proven FIRST, in a commit that precedes the compose flip: (a) the `infra/runbooks/` kill-switch
      entry, (b) the Bedrock `InvokeModel` client-error alarm, (c) an OBSERVED `OK → ALARM`
      transition of `rebar-gerrit-voter-errors` from an induced `VOTER_ERROR` while the bot is still on
      the Anthropic path, and (d) an OBSERVED successful `pydantic_ai.providers.bedrock` import INSIDE
      the rebuilt running container —
      `docker compose exec review-bot python -c "import pydantic_ai.providers.bedrock"` exiting 0, with
      the command and its exit status recorded — because the image's `uv sync` does not install the
      `bedrock` extra today (`Dockerfile.reviewbot:83`) and `bedrock_model.py:60-66` raises
      `LLMConfigError` without it, so a flip made first would be discovered as an outage of the gate that
      reviews every landing. A boto3-based Bedrock or region reachability probe does NOT satisfy (d) and
      must not be substituted for it: `pyproject.toml:93` puts boto3 in the image via the `reviewbot`
      extra regardless, so such a probe passes on an image that still lacks the provider module. The kill
      switch's own end-to-end execution is necessarily post-cutover and has
      its own criterion below.

- [ ] `infra/compose/docker-compose.yml`'s `review-bot` service sets `REBAR_LLM_FRONTIER_MODEL`,
      `REBAR_LLM_STANDARD_MODEL` and `REBAR_LLM_TRIVIAL_MODEL` to `bedrock:`-qualified inference-profile
      ids, and sets no `REBAR_LLM_MODEL`.

- [ ] `infra/compose/Dockerfile.reviewbot`'s `uv sync --locked` line installs the `bedrock` extra
      alongside `agents` and `reviewbot`, and the committed `uv.lock` is unchanged and still satisfies
      `--locked` (`uv lock --check` passes).

- [ ] a test asserts the three compose class-slot values are byte-equal to the corresponding entries in
      `.github/llm-providers/bedrock.toml`, and FAILS if either side is edited alone.

- [ ] a kill-switch entry exists under `infra/runbooks/` which (a) expresses the lever as the three
      class-slot env vars, naming `REBAR_LLM_MODEL` only to say it is a deprecated alias that must not be
      used here, (b) states that `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is deliberately RETAINED in the container so the
      lever has a credential, citing the shared-`.env`/opcert constraint
      (`fetch-secrets.sh:81,116`; `docker-compose.yml:113-114,196-197`), and (c) records the actual
      Bedrock retry/timeout posture — botocore stock client defaults, no rebar-configured retry envelope
      on this path (`bedrock_model.py:88`), and therefore `llm_retry_max_attempts` / `timeout_s` do NOT
      apply to Bedrock.

- [ ] the botocore retry/timeout parity gap is filed as its own ticket, linked `discovered_from` this
      one, with its id recorded in a comment here.

- [ ] a Bedrock `InvokeModel` client-error alarm is declared in `infra/terraform/` whose METRIC SOURCE and
      RATE COMPUTATION are explicit, not just its thresholds: a `metric_query` metric-math expression over
      the AWS/Bedrock native `InvocationClientErrors` and `Invocations` metrics, dimensioned by `ModelId`
      to match how AWS publishes them, with the epic's thresholds (client-error rate > 25% of invocations,
      15-minute period, 2 consecutive evaluation periods) present as literal values in the resource. The
      resource carries a METRIC SOURCE comment in the style of `monitoring_s4b.tf`/`monitoring_s5.tf`,
      noting that unlike those two this metric is AWS-published and so is dimensioned rather than
      dimensionless.
- [ ] the alarm is proven to be watching something that EXISTS rather than sitting in INSUFFICIENT_DATA:
      its state is recorded as `OK` (or `ALARM`) with a datapoint, not `INSUFFICIENT_DATA`, after real
      Bedrock traffic. An alarm on a metric nothing publishes is the failure mode this criterion exists to
      exclude, and it is indistinguishable from a healthy alarm by state name alone.

- [ ] [operator-attested] the Bedrock alarm's ARN and one FORCED test notification are recorded in a
      comment, so the epic's "alarm ARN + one forced test notification recorded on S8" evidence
      requirement is met rather than inherited unresolved.

- [ ] [operator-attested] `rebar-gerrit-voter-errors` is recorded transitioning `OK → ALARM` from an
      induced `VOTER_ERROR` on the pre-cutover Anthropic path, with the induction method stated (and
      NOT a closed change — see [rebar:c943-1b38-d613-4013]) and the observed timestamps.

- [ ] [operator-attested] a real Gerrit change receives an `LLM-Review` vote produced via Bedrock, with
      the change id and the vote recorded in a comment, and its sidecar provenance showing
      `provider == "bedrock"`. Prerequisite: [rebar:e951-7df6-1851-4d5e] must have landed, since the
      code-review gate does not stamp `provider_provenance` without it
